::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**The content has moved. The old site has not yet been turned into pointers.**
Every row of the inventory in Section 2 is resolved and all seven acceptance
checks passed on 2026-09-02. Section 3 holds what is left.

Cut from 803 lines to this on 2026-09-02, at Andy's instruction. The naming and
placement arguments, the Google Takeout export route, the navigation design and
the phase plan came out: each had either been executed or been overtaken by how
the work was actually done. What survives is the inventory, the acceptance
result, the old-URL problem, and the file and export mechanics that the build
still depends on.
:::

## 1. Goal and outcome

One site, at one URL, holding both what was on
`sites.google.com/site/andrewsteinphd` and what was on TrinityMetrics, with no
content dropped without a recorded decision to drop it.

The merged site keeps the name TrinityMetrics and the personal material became
a section rather than the site's title. The subject is ordered into three legs:
pharmacometrics, teaching and education, GenAI. Both decisions are now visible
on the site itself, so the argument for them has been removed from here.

Eleven pages and nineteen linked files came across between 2026-09-01 and
2026-09-02. No file was hosted on the old site: every one of the nineteen
already lived in `iamstein/Publications` or on the xgx site, so only the eleven
page URLs need pointers.

-   **LINK** --- not ported; the merged site links to the canonical copy

-   **DROP** --- deliberately not carried over. Requires a reason in the row.

## 3. What remains

Three pieces. None of them blocks the others.

**Publications has no page.** There is no `publications.qmd` and no
`publications.yml`. The design settled on: a YAML file plus a Quarto listing
matching `projects.yml`, each entry carrying title, authors, journal, year, DOI
and a link, with the `.bib` exported from Google Scholar and committed beside
it as a download. The YAML drives what a reader sees so the page looks like the
rest of the site; the `.bib` serves whoever wants to cite the work. The
duplication is bounded by publications arriving a few times a year, one at a
time.

**The domain is not wired to GitHub Pages, and `site-url` must not change until
it is.** Checked 2026-09-01: `trinitymetrics.com` answers with a 301 to
`https://iamstein.github.io/TrinityMetrics/`, its A records are `3.33.251.168`
and `15.197.225.128`, `www.trinitymetrics.com` does not resolve, and the
repository has no `CNAME` file. That is a registrar-level forward rather than a
custom domain, so a reader who types the domain ends with `iamstein.github.io`
in the address bar. Setting `site-url` to the domain now would point every
canonical URL, sitemap entry and RSS link at a forwarder. The order is: point
DNS at the GitHub Pages addresses `185.199.108.153` through `185.199.111.153`,
or `www` at `iamstein.github.io`; add a `CNAME` file holding the domain; set
the custom domain in the repository's Pages settings; wait for the certificate;
then correct `site-url`. The DNS step needs Andy's registrar login, and was
deferred by him on 2026-09-01 to be done as its own piece of work.

**The old site still serves its original content.** All eleven pages returned
200 with their full bodies on 2026-09-02. Section 5 says what to replace them
with and why the site should stay published afterwards.

## 4. Acceptance checks, and the result

Run on 2026-09-02. All seven pass.

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every inventory row has a disposition, and every DROP row a reason | ✅ 30 rows, none missing either |
| 2 | Dispositions sum to the recorded row count | ✅ 19 + 2 + 8 + 1 = 30 |
| 3 | A link check over the rendered `docs/` finds no broken internal link | ✅ 808 internal links, 0 broken |
| 4 | No page links to `sites.google.com/site/andrewsteinphd` as a live destination | ✅ hits only inside `projects/site-integration/`, where the address is the subject |
| 5 | Every file referenced from a ported page exists and is covered by `resources:` in `_quarto.yml` | ✅ none missing |
| 6 | No page on the old site is left half-migrated | ✅ all eleven serve their original content |
| 7 | The site renders and publishes from `publish.yml` with no manual step | ✅ three consecutive green runs |

**Check 6 passes before and after the work it is supposed to measure.** A page
showing its original content satisfies it, and so does a page replaced by a
pointer. Re-run this list once the pointers go up, and replace check 6 with one
that requires every old page to carry the new address. Nothing here tests
Section 3 either, so these seven checks can pass while the project is
unfinished.

The link check was a script over `docs/`; `lychee` and `linkchecker` are not
installed on this machine.

## 5. Old URLs and inbound links

Every old URL breaks unless something is done, and the ones that matter are
printed in places that cannot be edited: papers, conference bios, slide
footers, the Google Scholar profile, other people's link lists.

**Google Sites cannot redirect to an external site.** There is no redirect
feature and no server to configure. The workable substitute is to keep the old
site published and replace each page's body with a short pointer to the new
address, page by page, matching the Section 2 inventory. A reader following a
ten-year-old citation lands on a live page that tells them where to go.

**Do not delete the old site.** Not at the end of the migration, not a year
later. It costs nothing to leave a Google Site published and it is the only
thing standing between an old citation and a 404.

**Update what can be updated.** The Google Scholar profile's homepage field,
the GitHub profile, LinkedIn, ORCID, and any conference bio still within reach.
This is a short list and it catches most live traffic.

## 6. Files, decks and the Google Docs export

Files from the old site live in `files/`, listed under `resources:` in
`_quarto.yml` so Quarto copies them into `docs/` unrendered. The reference
documents the Resources page links stay in `references/`, which is listed
there too.

Naming is lower case, hyphens, no spaces, and a date prefix on anything with a
date attached: `2019-acop-poster.pdf`, not `ACoP Poster (final) v2.pdf`.

**PDFs are the ported form for slides.** A PowerPoint file on a static site is
a download rather than a page, and a reader on a phone cannot open it. Do not
commit the `.pptx` beside the `.pdf`: it doubles the storage, and git keeps
every version for the life of the repository.

### Size limits and compression

The binding limit is the 1 GB published Pages site rather than the 100 MB
per-file limit. A deck exported to PDF is nowhere near 100 MB; what could reach
1 GB is the sum. Compress before the first commit, because a file committed
uncompressed and recompressed later leaves both copies in the history
permanently.

```bash
gs -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dPDFSETTINGS=/ebook -dCompatibilityLevel=1.4 \
   -dNOPAUSE -dQUIET -dBATCH -sOutputFile=out.pdf in.pdf
```

Measured on `references/Uncertainty_Assessment_Presentation.pdf`, the 105-page
deck already in this repository: 14.8 MB at source, 2.5 MB at `/ebook`, 1.5 MB
at `/screen`, page count unchanged in both. On the most image-heavy page,
`/ebook` is indistinguishable from the source and `/screen` visibly softens the
small annotation labels. **Use `/ebook`.** At that ratio the 1 GB ceiling
arrives at roughly 400 decks.

### The build exports the Google Docs

`_scripts/export-google-docs.sh` fetches nine Docs as PDFs into `docs/files/`
after `quarto render`, and `publish.yml` calls it in one line. Readers on a
corporate network cannot open Google Docs, so every Doc the site links to is
published here as a PDF and linked beside the Google original. Nothing is
committed: the PDFs are written during the build and travel in the Pages
artifact, so they are never stale and never enter git history.

A Doc exports over plain HTTP while it is shared as **anyone with the link,
Viewer**, at `https://docs.google.com/document/d/DOC_ID/export?format=pdf`.
Slides use `/presentation/d/DOC_ID/export/pdf`.

**`curl --fail` does not catch a broken share setting.** A Doc that is not
link-shared returns 200 and serves Google's sign-in page. Measured 2026-09-02
on the three Drive files behind `software.qmd`: each returned about 907 KB of
`text/html` titled "Google Drive: Sign-in". The script checks that the first
four bytes of what it downloaded are `%PDF`, and deletes the file and fails the
build when they are not. Those three links stay pointing at Drive. Andy
2026-09-02: that is fine for the old software.

The export endpoint is not part of a documented API and Google could change it.
The build failing loudly is the detection mechanism; the fallback is to commit
a PDF by hand until it is fixed.
